options.content:
# Control links

Clicking a control cell sends a REST request to the mock control server (examples/controlServer) instead of opening a tab.

- **Pump 1 status / Pump 2 status**: GET the pump, and the response drives the cell label. Pump 1 is an object result, so its fields `pump1.state` and `pump1.level` are available.
- **Start pump 1 / Stop pump 1**: POST an action. Each response is placed on the time-slider at the time it arrived, and the value holds until the next response.
- **Reset all**: silent. The request is sent, nothing is shown, and any error only goes to the console.
- **Device fault**: the server answers HTTP 503. The cell shows the configured error text in red.
- **Slow device**: the server waits longer than the 1.5 s timeout. The cell shows the timeout as an error.

Start the server with `node examples/controlServer/server.mjs` and use the time-slider to step through the actions.

options.panelConfig:
---

#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Control links example. Requires the mock control server in examples/controlServer:
#   node examples/controlServer/server.mjs
#
# To run behind a same-origin proxy (e.g. Apache ProxyPass /control to the server),
# set controlBase to "" so the links become relative: "/control/pump/pump1".

cellIdPreamble: "cell-"
gradientMode: "hue"
cellLabelDecimalPoints: 0

linkVariables:
  controlBase: "http://localhost:8090"

cells:
  # A click refreshes the status from the server. The response is an object so the
  # fields 'pump1.state' and 'pump1.level' are available to drive the cell.
  pump1:
    link:
      url: "${controlBase}/control/pump/pump1"
      open: "result"
      method: "GET"
      resultDataRef: "pump1"
      resultPath: "pump"
      error:
        text: "STATUS ERR ${status}"
        color: "red"
    label:
      dataRef: "pump1.state"
      separator: "cr"

  pump2:
    link:
      url: "${controlBase}/control/pump/pump2"
      open: "result"
      method: "GET"
      resultDataRef: "pump2"
      resultPath: "pump"
      error:
        text: "STATUS ERR ${status}"
        color: "red"
    label:
      dataRef: "pump2.level"
      separator: "cr"
      units: "none"

  # 'silent' sends the request without showing a result. Errors only go to the console.
  resetAll:
    link:
      url: "${controlBase}/control/reset"
      open: "silent"
      method: "POST"
    label:
      separator: "cr"

  # Each action writes the new pump state to the 'pump1' result, so the pump1 cell
  # shows the change and the time-slider shows one step per action.
  startPump1:
    link:
      url: "${controlBase}/control/pump/pump1"
      open: "result"
      method: "POST"
      body:
        action: "start"
      resultDataRef: "pump1"
      resultPath: "pump"
      error:
        text: "ERR ${status}"
        color: "red"
    label:
      separator: "cr"

  stopPump1:
    link:
      url: "${controlBase}/control/pump/pump1"
      open: "result"
      method: "POST"
      body:
        action: "stop"
      resultDataRef: "pump1"
      resultPath: "pump"
      error:
        text: "ERR ${status}"
        color: "red"
    label:
      separator: "cr"

  # The server answers HTTP 503 for this action. The cell shows the error text
  # and the status, and the error is also logged to the console.
  failPump1:
    link:
      url: "${controlBase}/control/pump/pump1"
      open: "result"
      method: "POST"
      body:
        action: "fail"
      resultDataRef: "pump1"
      resultPath: "pump"
      error:
        text: "FAIL ${status} ${message}"
        color: "red"
    label:
      separator: "cr"

  # The server waits longer than the timeout, so the request fails with a timeout message.
  slowPump1:
    link:
      url: "${controlBase}/control/pump/pump1"
      open: "result"
      method: "POST"
      body:
        action: "slow"
      timeoutMs: 1500
      resultDataRef: "pump1"
      resultPath: "pump"
      error:
        text: "TIMEOUT ${message}"
        color: "red"
    label:
      separator: "cr"
